checkOutcomes.method: forced-colours screenshot plus Lighthouse contrast audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: Forced-colours mode preserves readable text, controls and boundaries; Lighthouse color-contrast scored 1.
DOM and stylesheet inspection across home, topic and story templates found no view-transition declarations or named transition elements.
No scroll-linked visual effect is present, and no animation-timeline or active animation was found, so the feed does not implement a main-thread scroll-animation anti-pattern.
The feed uses native document scrolling and ordinary links/buttons; no custom swipe, drag or pointer-driven interaction was present in the representative reading flow.
The 6,591 px home capture and 26,590 px topic DOM show very long listings, while DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, scroll progress indicator or adaptive header state.
No tooltip or detached floating menu is required for the primary signed-out reading flow; visible controls remain attached and unclipped in the captured states.
Descriptive topic links, story titles, section headings and See more headlines controls provide clear orientation from home to topic and story overview.
Navigating to https://news.google.com redirects to consent.google.com and replaces the feed with a full-page Before you continue decision surface.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM review of interruption and controls
checkOutcomes.evidence: The consent choice uses native buttons with explicit Reject all and Accept all actions; the news reading surfaces do not introduce custom modal divs in the exercised path.
The home, topic and story templates devote the main viewport to headlines and source context; application chrome is compact relative to the long content feed.
The mobile layout primitive reports visualViewportWidth 360, scrollWidth 1024 and horizontalOverflowPx 664; the full-page capture is 1024 px wide.
Computed styles on home, topic and story report container-type normal, and the captured CSS contains no @container rules; the narrow-viewport run falls back to a 1024 px layout.
The focus probe reports outline-style none on the first focusable anchor and five rendered links with heights from 12 to 20 px.
Google News, Your briefing, Top stories and source-labelled headlines make the page purpose and next reading actions explicit.
The exercised home, topic and multi-source story URLs loaded and exposed crawlable headline links without requiring sign-in.
Signed-out personalisation is clearly labelled with a Sign in action, while source and story states remain understandable; the separate HTTP failure weakness is recorded under resilience.
Lighthouse reports performance 0.41, FCP 6.0 s, LCP 10.1 s, TBT 830 ms and time to interactive 14.1 s. The raw-CDP trace corroborates LCP 2.78 s and one 188.83 ms long task in a less-throttled run.
The layout observer measured CLS 0 in the capture window and Lighthouse measured CLS 0.006.
Lighthouse measured 830 ms total blocking time and a 670 ms maximum potential input delay; the CDP trace found a 188.83 ms long task.

The HAR records 120 requests and 1.46 MB transferred, including 367 KB of fonts. The Google Fonts stylesheet is parser-inserted at VeryHigh priority; Lighthouse flags LCP discovery and network dependency failures.
Lighthouse estimates 352 KiB of unused JavaScript and 199 KiB of unused CSS on the audited load.
Lighthouse identifies Top stories and Local news anchors where aria-label is prohibited because the elements have no valid role in the computed accessibility model.
Lighthouse color-contrast scored 1 and forced-colours mode kept content readable.
Lighthouse fails heading-order for article h4 elements. ui-probe records h1 followed by h3 sections and six empty h3 elements; it also records no nav landmark.

checkOutcomes.method: desktop, mobile and high-contrast screenshot review
checkOutcomes.evidence: Headline and metadata text remains readable with clear grouping and no visible clipping on the representative templates, apart from the separately reported viewport overflow.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse viewport audit and mobile capture
checkOutcomes.evidence: The viewport meta audit passes and the page permits normal scaling; no essential audio/video requiring captions appeared. Target-size and horizontal reflow issues are separately recorded under input and form-factor checks.
Lighthouse errors-in-console scored 1 and reported no console error items.
Lighthouse doctype, charset, image-alt, aspect-ratio and deprecated API audits pass; observed CLS is low despite missing explicit img dimensions.
Lighthouse reports a large first-party script without a source map and three BFCache blockers, including cache-control: no-store on the main resource.
Home, topic and story each expose descriptive titles and meta descriptions.
Headline links have real href values, viewport meta passes, robots allows home/topics/stories for general crawlers, and Lighthouse SEO scores 1.

checkOutcomes.method: metadata, status, robots and sitemap inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited URLs return 200, expose canonical URLs, appear under allowed robots patterns, and the fetched sitemap is populated.
Home, topic and story expose Organization or page JSON-LD plus matching Open Graph title, URL, description and image metadata.
The headers primitive confirms HTTPS and nosniff, but finds no HSTS or Referrer-Policy and a CSP containing unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval.

The HAR attributes 83 of 120 requests and 1.12 MB of 1.46 MB transferred to other origins, including a 153 KB Google Tag Manager script. The tracker probe found no listed tracker match, but analytics collection appears in the HAR.
No geolocation, notification or media permission request was detected on load; the platform exposes WebAuthn and sign-in is optional for core reading.
The headers primitive confirms HTTPS and nosniff, but finds no HSTS or Referrer-Policy and a CSP containing unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval.
The discoverability primitive reports only 21% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML. Title, h1 and description survive, but the crawler screenshot contains only a small fraction of the rendered feed.
Home, topic and story templates reached stable rendered states with intact controls and no clipped primary overlays in the desktop captures.
A standalone web app manifest with icons and start_url is present, and a service worker controls the news origin.
The same-origin missing-route fetch failed with TypeError rather than returning a usable error document, while direct navigation was redirected to the consent surface instead of a contextual 404.
The document uses lang=en-GB and ltr direction; localized templates render coherently across home, topic and story.
The UK surface uses en-GB labels, Sunday 19 July, Celsius weather and locale-appropriate relative publication ages.
The audited reading surfaces contain relative publication ages but no scheduling, recurring-event or time-zone conversion flow.

findings.summary: The news experience ignores the requested dark colour scheme.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a light #f6f8fc surface; ui-probe reports prefers-color-scheme: dark matched while root color-scheme is normal and body text remains dark on a light background.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and derive surfaces, text, icons and browser chrome from prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: A full-page consent interstitial blocks the requested news content on first visit.
findings.evidence: Navigating to https://news.google.com redirects to consent.google.com and replaces the feed with a full-page Before you continue decision surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the equally prominent accept and reject choices, but use a compact, accessible consent surface where law and policy permit, preserving access to non-personalised core content.

findings.summary: The layout exposes a desktop-width canvas in a 360 px visual viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout primitive reports visualViewportWidth 360, scrollWidth 1024 and horizontalOverflowPx 664; the full-page capture is 1024 px wide.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the 1024 px minimum layout width, size the main grid intrinsically, and verify scrollWidth equals the visual viewport at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on the first focusable link and several links have undersized hit areas.
findings.evidence: The focus probe reports outline-style none on the first focusable anchor and five rendered links with heights from 12 to 20 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a clearly visible :focus-visible treatment and provide at least 24 by 24 CSS pixel target areas, preferably 44 by 44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is well outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports performance 0.41, FCP 6.0 s, LCP 10.1 s, TBT 830 ms and time to interactive 14.1 s. The raw-CDP trace corroborates LCP 2.78 s and one 188.83 ms long task in a less-throttled run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP content, reduce startup JavaScript, delay non-critical work and set a performance budget against throttled LCP and interaction latency.

findings.summary: Startup JavaScript blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 830 ms total blocking time and a 670 ms maximum potential input delay; the CDP trace found a 188.83 ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Break startup work into sub-50 ms tasks, schedule non-visible work at lower priority and defer modules until their UI is requested.

findings.summary: Font and script delivery delays the critical path.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 120 requests and 1.46 MB transferred, including 367 KB of fonts. The Google Fonts stylesheet is parser-inserted at VeryHigh priority; Lighthouse flags LCP discovery and network dependency failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset and self-host critical font faces where feasible, preload only the required face, streamline the critical dependency chain and defer non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: The home feed ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 352 KiB of unused JavaScript and 199 KiB of unused CSS on the audited load.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split feed, account, feedback and optional feature bundles; remove unused rules from the initial route and load optional dependencies conditionally.

findings.summary: Some headline links carry prohibited ARIA attributes.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies Top stories and Local news anchors where aria-label is prohibited because the elements have no valid role in the computed accessibility model.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a valid native anchor role with a real href and visible accessible text, removing ARIA that conflicts with the resulting role.

findings.summary: Heading levels skip from section headings to h4 article headlines, and multiple source headings are empty.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails heading-order for article h4 elements. ui-probe records h1 followed by h3 sections and six empty h3 elements; it also records no nav landmark.
findings.suggestedFix: Give sections a sequential h2 structure, make article heading levels follow their section, remove empty headings and expose the primary navigation as a nav landmark.

findings.summary: Large JavaScript lacks source maps and the page cannot use the back-forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a large first-party script without a source map and three BFCache blockers, including cache-control: no-store on the main resource.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish production source maps to authorised tooling and narrow no-store usage so non-sensitive news views can restore from BFCache.

findings.summary: The observed response weakens browser-enforced transport and script protections.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirms HTTPS and nosniff, but finds no HSTS or Referrer-Policy and a CSP containing unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval.
findings.suggestedFix: Send HSTS and a restrictive Referrer-Policy, remove unsafe-eval, and migrate remaining inline execution to nonces or hashes.

findings.summary: Third-party delivery and analytics dominate the initial transfer.
findings.evidence: The HAR attributes 83 of 120 requests and 1.12 MB of 1.46 MB transferred to other origins, including a 153 KB Google Tag Manager script. The tracker probe found no listed tracker match, but analytics collection appears in the HAR.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise analytics payload and collection, delay it until appropriate consent, consolidate same-operator origins where practical and budget third-party bytes.

findings.summary: Most live news content is unavailable to a browser or crawler without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: The discoverability primitive reports only 21% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML. Title, h1 and description survive, but the crawler screenshot contains only a small fraction of the rendered feed.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the primary headline list and topic links, then hydrate personalisation and live updates as enhancements.

findings.summary: Many rendered images lack intrinsic dimensions and small favicons are delivered oversized.
findings.evidence: The image probe finds 100 of 100 img elements without width and height attributes and 38 oversized images, commonly 96 px favicon resources displayed at 14 px. Runtime CLS was low, so the risk is primarily waste and future instability rather than observed shift.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width and height, request favicon sizes close to display size, retain responsive srcset for editorial images and lazy-load below-fold media consistently.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts and fonts consume a disproportionate share of a text-heavy news feed.
findings.evidence: Third-party origins account for 1.12 MB of 1.46 MB transferred; fonts consume 367 KB and Google Tag Manager 153 KB before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Set route-level budgets for third-party JavaScript and fonts, defer analytics and optional support code, and reduce font variants.

findings.summary: The public news surface is intentionally unavailable to major AI agents and exposes no structured action interface.
findings.evidence: robots.txt explicitly disallows GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, anthropic-ai, ClaudeBot and Claude-Web. Lighthouse reports an agentic-browsing score of 0.33 and no llms.txt recommendation; raw content coverage is 21%.
findings.suggestedFix: If agent access is an intended channel, define an explicit crawler policy and expose safe read/search/follow capabilities through structured agent tools rather than scraping.

findings.summary: A missing same-origin route did not provide a useful recoverable error response in the exercised client context.
findings.evidence: The same-origin missing-route fetch failed with TypeError rather than returning a usable error document, while direct navigation was redirected to the consent surface instead of a contextual 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 status with a lightweight Google News error page, home/search recovery links and offline-aware retry messaging.

findings.summary: Template changes use abrupt full-state swaps rather than declarative view transitions.
findings.evidence: DOM and stylesheet inspection across home, topic and story templates found no view-transition declarations or named transition elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for feed-to-topic state changes and cross-document transitions where navigation remains on Google News, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The long feed offers no scroll-state progress or adaptive chrome.
findings.evidence: The 6,591 px home capture and 26,590 px topic DOM show very long listings, while DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, scroll progress indicator or adaptive header state.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a subtle scroll progress or section-position affordance and adapt sticky chrome with CSS scroll-state queries where supported.

findings.summary: Reusable feed cards do not expose container-driven responsive behaviour.
findings.evidence: Computed styles on home, topic and story report container-type normal, and the captured CSS contains no @container rules; the narrow-viewport run falls back to a 1024 px layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Make card and rail wrappers query containers and adapt card media, metadata and columns to their allocated inline size, independent of the viewport.
